chunks: From him, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Mas'ruq, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to a man who came to him: 'Shall I guide you to a matter by which Allah will admit you to Paradise?' He said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Give from what Allah has given you.' He said: 'But what if I am more in need than the one to whom I give?' He said: 'Then help the oppressed.' He said: 'And what if I am weaker than the one I help?' He said: 'Then deal with the silly one (al-akhrak), meaning, indicate upon him (his affairs).' He said: 'What if I am sillier than the one I do this for?' He said: 'Then silence your tongue except from goodness.' Would it not please you that there should be a characteristic from these characteristics in you, pulling you to Paradise?

key_terms.أَشِرْ عَلَيْهِ: Indicate upon him / point out to him
key_terms.أَنِلْ: Give from what is given to you (charity/giving)
key_terms.الْأَخْرَقِ: The silly/foolish one (a specific term used in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the hierarchy of good deeds from giving wealth to controlling the tongue according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines a descending hierarchy of spiritual effort, culminating in 'silence of the tongue' (samt al-lisan) as the most accessible and foundational virtue for all believers, regardless of their capacity for wealth or strength. Shia scholars emphasize this progression as a practical guide for self-purification (tazkiyah), where guarding one's speech is the prerequisite for higher acts of justice and charity. The narration underscores that even the simplest act of speaking only good serves as a direct conduit to Paradise, highlighting the centrality of verbal discipline in Shia ethical teachings.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Al Haysam Bin Abu Masrouq, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to a man who had come to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Shall I<sup>saww</sup> point you upon a matter that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Enter you into the Pradise due to it?’ He said, ‘Yes, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Give from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Gave you’. He said, ‘Supposing I am more needy than the one I give it to?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So help the oppressed’. He said, ‘And if I was weaker than the one I help?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So, deal with the silly one, meaning, indicate upon him (his affairs)’. He said, ‘Supposing I was more silly than the one I do (this) for’. He said, ‘So silence your tongue except from goodness. Would it not cheer you that there should be a characteristic from these characteristics in you, pulling you to the Paradise?’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from al-Haytham ibn abu Masruq from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah said to a man who had come to see him, ‘Should I guide you to a matter with which Allah will enter you in paradise?’ The man said, ‘Yes, O Messenger of Allah.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Give of what Allah has given you.’ The man asked, ‘What if I were more needy than the recipient?’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Then help the oppressed.’ The man asked, ‘What if I were weaker than the oppressed?’ The Messenger of Allah then said, ‘Do what an ignorant person may do, that is, guide him to good.’ The man asked, ‘What if I were more ignorant than him?’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Control your tongue except from good. Do you not like to have one of the above mentioned qualities in you that may lead you to paradise?”’
